candidates.title: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
candidates.content: π^4 is a unified foundation model for 4D scene perception. From diverse, uncalibrated RGB observations in the wild---a single image, an unordered collection, or a video sequence---it recovers dense geometry, camera poses, and metric scale, together with 2D/3D point tracks and moving-object masks for multi-image inputs. It couples a geometry branch with a geometry-conditioned motion branch, which predicts image-space correspondences that are lifted into 3D using reconstructed target-view geometry. Across diverse benchmarks, π^4 achieves the best overall average rank in geometry evaluation, alongside competitive performance in single- and multiview 2D/3D point tracking and moving-object segmentation. With a shared backbone, the full geometry-and-motion system contains approximately 0.5B parameters---less than half the size of most baselines. It produces joint reconstructions and tracks in one forward pass, including large-scale scenes with thousands of input images despite training with contexts of at most 64 views. We further present the data and training recipe underlying these capabilities, together with empirical studies of key design choices. Code and models are available at htt

candidates.title: MPEG-Diffusion: Mixed-Resolution Video Generation
candidates.content: Video diffusion transformers (DiTs) generate realistic videos, but their heavy computational cost limits broader real-world applications. Mixed-resolution generation reduces this cost by generating the visually important region at high resolution (HR) and the rest at low resolution (LR), yet existing methods suffer a severe quality drop on videos and require knowing the HR region in advance. We show that these failures are not inherent to mixed resolution, and propose MPEG-Diffusion to address their three root causes: (1) dual-resolution attention to mitigate the curse of mixed resolution, where each query reads the K/V of its own resolution, (2) a mixed-resolution decoder to blend the HR and LR latents before decoding and resolve distortion, and (3) a self-selected HR region using the DiT's knowledge to find the visually important region without requiring it in advance. Processing only 30% of full-resolution tokens, MPEG-Diffusion speeds up denoising by 4.8times on Wan2.1 14B (3.8times on 1.3B), outperforming prior methods on nearly every metric. candidates.title: Regularized Score Centering
candidates.content: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. To stabilize off-policy learning, score centering (SC) removes the effect of reward baselines on the expected update. Our gradient diagnostics show less extreme gradients with SC than with importance sampling (IS), but SC can still fail when the learner moves far from the behavior policy that generated the data. To limit this policy mismatch, we introduce Regularized Score Centering (RSC), which adds a reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) penalty to encourage the learner's next-token distribution to stay close to the behavior policy's next-token distribution. RSC works with or without truncated importance sampling (TIS), which caps token importance weights. Our theoretical analysis supports this approach, showing that KL regularization improves convergence guarantees. We evaluate dense and mixture-of-experts models on mathematical reasoning and agentic tasks, including online shopping, tool use, games, and fully asynchronous software engineering. candidates.title: Risk Stratification in Lean MASLD
candidates.content: Evaluation of metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) relies on the “visible proxy” of body size. This is understandable: excess adiposity, associated with insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, and cardiometabolic dysfunction, is a major driver of the global MASLD epidemic. Yet this framing becomes misleading when body mass index (BMI) is treated as a surrogate for metabolic risk. A clinically important minority of patients develop MASLD despite a BMI in the normal range. These patients, commonly described as having lean MASLD, reveal the limitations of an obesity-centered clinical approach and ultimately challenge the assumption that normal body weight implies low liver-related risk.

candidates.title: Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillators for Patients With an LVEF >35%
candidates.content: The implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) remains a cornerstone therapy for the prevention of sudden cardiac death. Randomized clinical trials have demonstrated a survival benefit with ICDs for primary prevention in patients with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35% or less; therefore, professional guideline recommendations on ICDs are based on this LVEF cutoff. However, most individuals who experience a sudden cardiac arrest do not have significant left ventricular dysfunction. Admittedly, these LVEF cutoffs are arbitrary, and the risk of sudden cardiac death is not dichotomous.

candidates.title: Live-cell imaging reveals two modes of TERRA association with telomeres and the dynamics of TERRA R-loops
candidates.content: Abstract Telomeres are transcribed into TERRA long non-coding RNAs. When associating with telomeres, TERRA can regulate telomere maintenance by semiconservative DNA replication, telomerase and homology-directed repair (HDR). In addition, TERRA alters telomeric structure and protein composition. Yet, the molecular mechanisms and dynamics by which TERRA associates with telomeres remain elusive. To investigate TERRA-telomere interactions, we combine PP7 stem-loop TERRA tagging, genome editing and live-cell imaging. Using a deep-learning method for spot detection and single-particle tracking analysis, we demonstrate that TERRA associates with telomeres through two distinct modes. On one hand, TERRA interacts frequently and transiently with the telomeric shelterin protein TRF2. On the other hand, TERRA engages in long-lasting interactions which persist from seconds to several minutes forming R-loops with telomeric DNA. TERRA R-loops preferentially occur at short telomeres, and their formation requires factors involved in HDR, but not TRF2. candidates.title: A non-nucleotide activator reveals a second allosteric regulatory site in the type III CRISPR ribonuclease Csm6
candidates.content: Abstract Type III CRISPR-Cas systems rely on cyclic oligoadenylate (cOA) signaling to activate ancillary nucleases such as Csm6, which serve as core effectors in antiviral immunity. While cOA-mediated Csm6 activation has been widely harnessed for molecular diagnostics, its broader application is constrained by inherent limitations, including poor cellular permeability and susceptibility to degradation by ring nucleases. Here, we conducted a high-throughput fluorescence-based screen and identified DMPCH (7,8-dimethyl-4-phenylchroman-2-one) as a non-nucleotide allosteric activator of Thermus thermophilus ( Tt ) Csm6. DMPCH selectively stimulates Tt Csm6 ribonuclease activity by binding to the higher eukaryotes and prokaryotes nucleotide-binding domain dimerization interface, leading to expansion of the catalytic pocket and remodeling of the R-X 4–6 -H catalytic motif. Moreover, DMPCH acts synergistically with cA 4 to activate Tt Csm6, enabling rapid and sensitive RNA detection in a Cas13a–Csm6 system. candidates.title: A dual biocontainment system specifically constraining the transfer and escape of the engineered plasmid in microbial communities
candidates.content: Abstract A variety of engineered genetic elements and circuits enable bacteria to sense environmental signals, process information, and execute programmed biological functions. However, the potential escape from such synthetic constructs into the natural environment poses biosafety risks and could disrupt ecological balance. To address this, we developed a dual biocontainment system designed to restrict the replication and expression of engineered plasmids exclusively within modified host (TEV protease and sgRNA-dCas9). This system employs TEV protease to remove ssrA degradation tags fused to the plasmid replication protein RepA, thereby enabling plasmid replication. Concurrently, a specific guide RNA (sgRNA) forms an inhibitory complex with dCas9 to prevent cleavage of the engineered plasmid by the I-OnuI endonuclease. Overall, dual biocontainment system provides a robust safety tool both in vitro and in vivo to restrict the transfer and escape of engineered plasmids (with an escape rate of 4.4 × 10 −8 in vitro and 2.4 × 10 −8 in vivo ), giving an efficient platform for safely use of synthetic genetic elements.

candidates.title: CDK phospho-degron tags for dynamic protein regulation
candidates.content: Cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) activity underpins cell cycle progression through dynamic and temporally ordered phosphorylation events. While transcriptional regulation has been extensively exploited in synthetic biology, the rational engineering of post-translational signaling circuits remains underdeveloped. Here, we introduce modular CDK-responsive phospho-degron tags derived from the Far1 regulatory region and demonstrate their ability to confer tunable, cell cycle-dependent control over protein stability in budding yeast. By systematically modifying cyclin docking motifs and Cks1 priming sites, we generate degron variants with distinct degradation kinetics and phosphorylation thresholds. These modules enable predictable modulation of transcription factor abundance and downstream gene expression. We further combine CDK-responsive degrons with phosphorylation-controlled localization modules for multi-layered regulation of sequential nuclear import and degradation. We encode multiple kinase activity thresholds within a single protein, demonstrating how complex phosphorylation logic can be compactly implemented. candidates.title: Precision in Predicting Catalytic Performance of Medium Chain Dehydrogenase: A Benchmark Data Set and Comparative Metrics
candidates.content: Medium-chain dehydrogenases/reductases are highly versatile oxidoreductases with broad industrial relevance but complex structure-function relationships that continue to challenge catalytic performance prediction. A Benchmark for Medium-Chain Dehydrogenases (MCDBench) is introduced as a rigorously curated benchmark dataset comprising 792 enzyme-substrate-cofactor combinations, including experimentally validated inactive cases obtained under standardized conditions. MCDBench spans 36 chemically diverse alcohol substrates, representative MDR subclasses, and multiple cofactor types, enabling systematic evaluation of model generalization. Benchmarking four representative activity-prediction models (DLKcat, UniKP, TurNuP, and CataPro) shows that correlations with experimental activities remain modest under standardized conditions, and that distinguishing active from inactive catalytic space remains a practical challenge across enzyme classes and substrate types. Analysis points to a positive-data skew inherited from widely used biochemical databases and the relative scarcity of validated negative samples as key factors shaping this behavior. candidates.title: Development of a Temperature-Based Method for Repeated Markerless Gene Integration in cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942
candidates.content: Genetic engineering of cyanobacteria can require multiple rounds of genome modification, highlighting the need for flexible markerless engineering tools. Here, we established a temperature-based markerless gene integration method using the temperature-sensitive H1 strain of Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942, which, unlike the wild-type strain, cannot grow at 40 {degrees}C. Disruption of nynA, encoding a putative endoribonuclease, allowed H1 to grow at 40 {degrees}C, enabling transformants with genes integrated at the nynA locus to be selected without an antibiotic-resistance marker. Complementation of nynA at a separate genomic locus restored temperature sensitivity, allowing the same selection principle to be reused. Using this strategy, gfp, mScarlet, and luciferase were sequentially integrated, with all three genes retained and expressed. To demonstrate its applicability to metabolic engineering, markerless integration of cnsA, encoding cineole synthase, enabled 1,8-cineole production at 81.4 {+/-} 9.52 {micro}g /g wet cell weight. This strategy enables repeated markerless genome modification in the H1 strain using temperature-based selection.

candidates.title: Obesity and Starvation
candidates.content: The essence of the successful method for reducing weight … lies in keeping the intake of energy below that of the output. Theoretically, complete fasting constitutes the most prompt method of accomplishing the end sought. It is a well-recognized fact, however, that starvation prolonged over a period of more than a few days, either voluntarily or as an incident of disease, may lead to unpleasant symptoms. Headache, nausea and dizziness portend the existence of conditions that are not exactly normal, and frequently they can be made to disappear promptly by the ingestion of even a little food. Most modern “treatments” for obesity, therefore, consist in underfeeding rather than complete fasting, particular care being directed to conserving the protein of the body so that the reduction in weight shall represent essentially a loss of body fat oxidized to furnish energy to the underfed individual.

candidates.title: Medicare and Bureau of Health Workforce and Funded Primary Care Residency Positions
candidates.content: To the Editor We are writing about the Research Letter “Changes in Specialty and Geography of Medicare’s New Residency Positions,” which reported that Medicare-funded expansion has not substantially increased primary care or rural training capacity. However, we would like to highlight an important limitation of specialty-based workforce estimates: residency positions labeled as primary care may not accurately reflect the production of physicians who enter primary care practice. Because these estimates rely on specialty designation, they may overstate primary care workforce contributions and fail to capture graduates’ postresidency practice.

candidates.title: Mandarin Wh-Indefinites Follow Nonveridicality in Multilingual LLMs, Unlike English any
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.20062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multilingual LLMs learn mostly from English. Do they carry English polarity licensing over to other languages? English any is licensed by downward-entailing (DE) contexts, Mandarin wh-indefinites such as shenme 'what/something' by nonveridical ones, and the two classes come apart: perhaps licenses shenme but not any, while only licenses any but entails existence. We test this dissociation in a pre-registered study of twelve open LLMs (0.5B-9B, four families), using 48 matched bilingual frames in 21 contexts and a log-probability difference-in-differences normalised by negation. All 11 models that pass the measurement gate license Mandarin wh-indefinites under possibility, necessity and evidential adverbs, at 0.42-2.33 times the strength of negation, while English any gets nothing in the same contexts. An exploratory extension to Qwen2.5-32B shows the same. candidates.title: Safety-Preserving Medical LLM Fine-Tuning via Bilevel Data Selection
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.20643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As general large language models (LLMs) are increasingly adapted for patient-facing medical applications, improving medical capability while controlling patient-facing risks remains a critical challenge. Large-scale medical instruction data are essential for acquiring domain knowledge through supervised fine-tuning (SFT), but unsafe responses can undermine existing safety alignment. To address this problem, we propose Scalable Bilevel Data Selection (S-BDS) for safety-preserving medical SFT. By controlling selection-weight concentration, S-BDS enables reliable sample ranking over large candidate pools and identifies training examples that improve medical capability while controlling patient-facing risks. We combine clinician-validated safe data and selected data with unscreened medical instruction data for SFT, and jointly evaluate medical capability and patient-facing safety on HealthBench and PatientSafetyBench, respectively. Experiments across Llama and Qwen models show that S-BDS achieves the highest safe rates among all compared methods, outperforming the strongest baselines by 4.64 and 3.00 percentage points, respectively, while

candidates.title: Navital Gym: Rule-Graded Agent Environments for Indian Workflows
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.20924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are being deployed on Indian workflows such as payments, tax, forms, travel and customer support in Hindi and Hinglish. Public agent evaluations rarely cover these workflows, and many score with another language model. We present Navital Gym, a set of six open environments with 321 public tasks in five task families: trip planning, UPI payments and disputes, GST invoicing and returns, form filling (including a multi-document split) and customer support in Hindi, Hinglish and three experimental Indian languages. Every task is graded by named, deterministic rules that recompute the outcome from a synthetic sandbox world. No language model judges any score. We report one run per task for three models on all six environments, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 4.5, and for Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite on two (UPI and the Support core). Opus solves 315 of 321 tasks, Sonnet 302 and Haiku 205. Trip planning and Hindi/Hinglish support separate the models most. candidates.title: MemeEconomy: Do LLM Agents Trade Ethics for Survival?
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.18908v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Alignment-trained large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in autonomous, multi-round settings where ethical compliance can come into direct tension with task success. While safety literature extensively documents failure modes like sycophancy and reward hacking, it largely overlooks a critical vulnerability: how agents behave under simulated existential economic pressure. We introduce MemeEconomy, a multimodal agentic market simulation in which LLM agents act as meme investors. Agents select content from a five-tier harm taxonomy and target communities under low-pressure and high-pressure (survival) environments. Each decision is logged in a Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) schema that we use as a diagnostic instrument, externalizing the agent's event understanding, declared priorities, and harm acknowledgment. Across ten models from four frontier model families, harmful selection rates remain consistently high and rise by +15 percentage points on average under an economic survival incentive. candidates.title: AI Agents May Always Fall for Prompt Injections
candidates.content: arXiv:2605.17634v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Prompt injection is the most critical vulnerability in deployed AI agents. Despite recent progress, we show that the prevailing defense paradigm (data-instruction separation) both fails to detect attacks that operate through contextual manipulation and degrades contextually appropriate behavior. We then recast prompt injection via the lens of Contextual Integrity (CI), a privacy theory that judges information flow compliance with contextual norms. This explains types of attacks that current defenses attempt to patch and predict advanced ones future agents will face. We develop unique benign and attack scenarios that force an agent to violate the norms by (1) misrepresenting the flow, (2) manipulating norms, or (3) mixing multiple flows. This reframing suggests an impossibility argument: an adversary can always construct a context under which a blocked flow appears legitimate, or a defender who tightens norms will block genuinely legitimate flows. Our findings suggest that current research addresses a shrinking fraction of future attack surfaces. Instead, through CI, we offer a principled framework for evaluating context-sens

candidates.title: Dynamic Shaping: Acquiring Interfaces and Constructing Execution over Frozen Pretrained Components
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.20573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Dynamic Shaping, a method for constructing executable neural arrangements through acquired response and partial-derivative interfaces over frozen pretrained components. The method learns local descriptions of available computation, ranks component rebindings using task-gradient alignment, transports the current interface across a rebinding, and retains changes through behavioral feedback. Continuous interface acquisition uses proximal policy optimization; the source coefficients remain fixed. We derive an exact identity relating transport error in component responses and partials to changes in action logits and their sensitivities. A pixels-only ViZDoom Basic study evaluates first task acquisition without a competent reference controller, demonstrations or intact response targets. Across three initializations and 100 shared held-out game seeds, initial arrangements succeed on 86/300 controller/episode pairs; joint interface-and-binding construction succeeds on 295/300. candidates.title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.13034v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Useful practice depends on the agent's current capabilities, so the procedure that chooses practice must also be revisable. We present RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models. The curriculum harness uses accumulated capability evidence to propose informative challenges, while the execution harness responds with reusable revisions that expand execution capabilities. Alternating updates hold one side fixed as the other changes, and admitted challenges form fixed snapshots for comparing execution revisions. Starting from a compact set of LIBERO practice conditions, the resulting frozen deployment outperforms the evaluated controllers and agent systems across four LIBERO-family panels. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 74.0% success, exceeding the initial deployment by 15.0 percentage points and direct execution by its VLA controller by 13.5 points. Case studi

candidates.title: CARET: Clinical Assertion-Aware Residual Calibration for Medical Image-Text Alignment
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.18811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Medical vision--language models align radiographs with free-text reports, but radiology language distinguishes explicit findings, negation, uncertainty, and omission. Treating these report states as interchangeable during feature adaptation can change image predictions without supporting visual evidence. We introduce CARET, a parameter-efficient image-side adaptation method that retains pretrained image and text encoders and uses paired positive and negative clinical statements to define a low-dimensional semantic correction space. A bounded residual adjusts image features along these directions, while assertion-aware supervision distinguishes explicitly present and absent findings from uncertain or unmentioned ones. At inference, the adapter requires only an image; textual references remain fixed. In zero-shot classification, CARET achieves 67.80\% accuracy on CheXpert 5$\times$200 and 65.20\% on RSNA. These scores exceed the published CLEFT-LoRA results by 1.06 and 0.27 percentage points, respectively. Comparisons to literature baselines are informative but not controlled for differences in pretraining and evaluation protocols. Ab

candidates.title: Effects of Conventional, Adaptive, and AI-Powered Upscaling on the Legibility of License Plates
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.18949v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Small details in digital images -- a face, a street sign, a license plate -- are routinely upscaled in hopes of making them interpretable. Upscaling options now range from conventional interpolation, whose operations are spatially invariant and fully explainable, to AI-powered methods that synthesize detail potentially absent from the source. Here, we ask which of these techniques most reliably helps human readers. In two online experiments, we measured legibility of 255 US license plates ranging in resolution from 128 to 8 pixels tall, as well as their legibility after upscaling by eight different methods. Legibility of the un-upscaled plates collapsed from ceiling to floor across a narrow band of plate heights (32 to 10 pixels). Conventional upscaling techniques (bilinear, bicubic, and Lanczos interpolation) gave modest gains of about 5-9 percentage points within this range. Nearest-neighbor interpolation, however, was harmful, rendering unreadable many plates that were readable without any upscaling. candidates.title: The CYBER-BRIDGE project: An AI-Powered Platform for Cross-Border Cybersecurity, Compliance and Forensics in the EU
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.21497v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cross-border cyber attacks on European SMEs and critical-infrastructure operators expose a structural cyber-resilience gap: cybersecurity (threat sharing, detection, response), compliance (framework assessment, certification) and digital forensics (cross-jurisdictional evidence) are jointly regulated by NIS2, the CRA, GDPR and the LED, yet their tooling evolved in silos and rarely interoperates across Member States. The EU-funded CYBER-BRIDGE project integrates the three domains under one architecture and a hash-chained evidence layer: AI-driven CTI sharing with ENISA-aligned notification, multi-framework assessments with retrieval-augmented advisory, and RFC 3161-anchored custody with lawful GDPR/LED exchange, all aligned with MITRE ATT&CK. A sanitised replica of the back-end image hosts a Cyber-Range for upskilling. candidates.title: NeuronGen: Neural Network Parameter Generation via Large Language Models
candidates.content: arXiv:2505.12470v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Acquiring the parameters of neural networks (NNs) has been one of the most important problems in machine learning since the inception of NNs. Traditional approaches, such as backpropagation and forward-only optimization, acquire parameters via iterative data fitting to gradually optimize them. This paper aims to explore the feasibility of a new direction: acquiring NN parameters via large language model generation. We propose NeuronGen, a generalized and easy-to-implement two-stage approach for NN parameter generation conditioned on descriptions of the data, task, and network architecture. Stage one is Parameter Reference Knowledge Injection, where LLMs are pretrained on NN checkpoints to build foundational understanding of parameter space, whereas stage two is Context-Enhanced Instruction Tuning, enabling LLMs to adapt to specific tasks through enriched, task-aware prompts. Experimental results demonstrate that NeuronGen effectively generates usable NN parameters. Our findings highlight the feasibility of LLM-based NN parameter generation and suggest a promising new paradigm where LLMs and lightweight NNs can coexist synergistica

candidates.title: Infrastructure-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Attention for Highway Ramp Merging
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.20078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-ramp merging is a typical safety and throughput problem on highways. Without proper coordination, human drivers and self-interested autonomous vehicles may make risky manoeuvres and cause accidents or congestion. With recent advances in connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), vehicles can be trained to coordinate for safe and efficient merging. However, in dense traffic, forming an effective observation of the traffic state is challenging. For example, observing only the neighbouring vehicles may lead to locally optimal decisions, while observing the entire traffic can introduce much irrelevant information. In this paper, we propose a transformer-based MARL vehicle control model to address these problems. A roadside infrastructure controller receives the states of all CAVs via vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communication and sends control commands back to them. An attention-based observation encoder is designed where each vehicle can filter the relevant vehicle information from the global traffic state. candidates.title: UrbanROI: Causal Modeling for Regional ROI Forecasting under POI Entry
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.20180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As urban commercial environments continue to evolve rapidly, accurately modeling the economic impact of point of interest (POI) entry is essential for supporting data-driven advertising allocation, merchant onboarding, and regional business decision-making. Existing return on investment (ROI) prediction methods mainly focus on individual ads or merchants, overlooking the interaction effects among POIs and failing to capture the causal influence of structural changes in urban commercial ecosystems. In this paper, we introduce a novel research problem -- regional ROI forecasting under POI entry, which aims to predict the future ROI trajectory of a commercial region after the introduction of a new POI by modeling temporal ROI evolution and competition-driven interactions among surrounding POIs. To address these challenges, we propose UrbanROI, an intervention-aware causal forecasting framework for region-level economic outcome prediction.
